units.translation: And now let it be, and let it not be a care to you.
And let no man-slaying destruction come upon us.
May I not be idle – may I not sin.
May I not be joined in marriage to any husband from heaven.
May the inescapable eye of gods stronger than I not look upon me.
May I not see this city running through the streets.
May the dust not drink and snatch away.
May strife not stain the ground of the land with native corpses.
May Ares not cut down the flower.
May marriage not come under compulsion.
But I care less for Zeus than for nothing.
Things that are of no help.
I am hopeful that you will be no less strong than Zeus.
Having given an oath that they would say nothing unjust.
Who, nurturing his heart in nothing in the light (Auratus: in fear)?
For who among mortals, fearing nothing, is just?
To admire nothing of the gods.
Will you not be silent? Will you say none of these things throughout the city?
And indeed, tell each of these things not in riddles, but plainly.
Do not pray for the fate of death.
Let him not boast of anything in Hades.
Let us not be stained with blood.
Know that you are not yet in the preludes.
Know well that the evil is not yet at its midpoint.
If the army is greater than the Median (or: if it is increasing?).
What arts and devices I devised.
He is devising a great evil in this house.
The daughter of Thestius devised a fire-kindling forethought.
And she who devised this abomination against her husband.
Subdued by the wrathful counsels of Hera.
In the singular number, fr. 450 in elegy, where it is about the Persian army defeated by the Greeks in the battle of Marathon, deep-haired Mede.
For Medus was the first leader of the army, where Medus seems to have the meaning of a proper name rather than a gentile adjective, as the scholiast believed: on which see Hermann's note.
No longer shooting arrows at us with his bow.
May old murder no longer breed in the house.
and such an army (of Greeks) having done many evils to the Medes
Having completed a long length of time.
the length of a yearly watch, corrupted from μῆχος, which see.
And there is no length in the middle of time.
And one will know the words in length.
I extended such a length of speech.
There was a double spelling of this adjective, Μαλιεύς [Malian] and, which alone the tragedians use, Μηλιεύς [Malian]. On both see Thes. vol. 5 p. 991.
The Dorian land and the Malian gulf, where Spercheius waters the plain with kindly drink.
Staining the altars of the gods with sheep.
The sheep already stand for slaughter.
